questions.stem: Archimedes' principle states that the buoyant force on an object equals the weight of:

options.option_text: The fluid displaced by the object

questions.explanation: Archimedes — the upward buoyant force equals the weight of the fluid displaced. An object floats if it can displace an amount of fluid equal to its own weight without being fully submerged. Iron ships float because their hollow hull displaces far more water than their metal weight. Hydrogen balloons rise because air displaced weighs more than the balloon + gas inside.

questions.stem: Hydraulic lifts and car brakes work on the principle of:
questions.explanation: Pascal's law — pressure applied to a confined fluid is transmitted equally in all directions. Small force on a small piston → amplified force on a large piston (because pressure P = F/A is equal; so F₂ = P × A₂ is larger where A₂ is larger). Used in hydraulic jacks, car brakes, hydraulic presses, steering. Bernoulli — pressure drop where flow speeds up (explains aircraft lift). Archimedes — buoyancy.

questions.stem: The atmospheric pressure at sea level is approximately:
questions.explanation: Standard atmospheric pressure at sea level — 101,325 Pa ≈ 101 kPa ≈ 1 atm ≈ 1,013 millibars ≈ 760 mmHg. Pressure drops with altitude — roughly halves every 5.5 km. On Everest (8.8 km), pressure is only ~33 kPa, which is why supplemental oxygen is usually needed above 8 km.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: The first mercury barometer, a device to measure atmospheric pressure, was invented by:
questions.explanation: Torricelli — Italian physicist, student of Galileo — invented the mercury barometer in 1643. A sealed glass tube inverted in a dish of mercury stands with the mercury column ~760 mm high at sea level — held up by atmospheric pressure pushing on the exposed mercury. The unit 'torr' (1 mmHg) is named after him. Pascal later replicated the experiment and showed pressure falls with altitude.

questions.stem: The reason why an aircraft wing generates lift is most directly explained by:
questions.explanation: Bernoulli — faster-moving fluid has lower pressure. An aircraft wing (aerofoil) is shaped so that air moves faster over the top and slower underneath → pressure on top is lower than on the bottom → net upward lift. Angle-of-attack and Newton's third law (wing redirects air downward → reaction upwards) also contribute. Archimedes is for static buoyancy in fluids; Pascal's law is for transmitted pressure in confined fluids.

questions.stem: The SI unit of pressure is named after:
questions.explanation: The pascal (Pa) — 1 N/m² — is the SI unit of pressure, named after Blaise Pascal (1623-62, French mathematician / physicist / philosopher). 101 kPa ≈ 1 atmosphere. Other named SI units — newton (force), joule (energy), hertz (frequency), ampere (current), volt (potential), ohm (resistance), farad (capacitance), henry (inductance), tesla (magnetic flux density), weber (magnetic flux), watt (power).

questions.stem: Water pressure at the bottom of a 10-metre-deep tank of still water is approximately (ρg ≈ 10,000):
questions.explanation: Gauge pressure at depth h = ρ × g × h. Water density ρ = 1,000 kg/m³; g = 10 m/s² (approx); h = 10 m. P = 1000 × 10 × 10 = 100,000 Pa = 100 kPa. Every 10 m depth in water adds ~1 atmosphere of pressure. At 100 m depth, gauge pressure is ~10 atm — which is why deep-sea diving is so limited without special equipment.
